harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s invoice exporter. It now uses private destination-local temporary files, atomically replaces outputs, cleans up on exit, and safely handles concurrent exports and symlinks. Source data, sentinel, OS release, and kernel were preserved. The repair survived a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Replaced the shared fixed temporary pathname with mktemp-created private files.
Added exit and signal cleanup traps.
Used an atomic destination-local rename so failures preserve existing output.
Removed the hostile legacy temporary symlink without modifying its target.
Verified normal, concurrent, symlink-attack, forced-failure, and cleanup behavior before and after reboot.
Restarted node1 once and confirmed a changed boot identity and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Successful exports retain all invoice rows
evidence.summary: Exports exactly matched invoices.csv and retained both invoice rows before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Concurrent exports use private temporary files
evidence.summary: The installed utility uses mktemp; 32 concurrent distinct/shared-destination exports passed before restart and 16 concurrent exports passed afterward.
Captured the original hostile symlink, then proved both the legacy temporary symlink and an output symlink could not redirect writes to protected.txt.
Forced final-rename failures left prior destination hashes unchanged before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Temporary files are removed on exit
evidence.summary: Successful, concurrent, and failed executions left zero temporary-file artifacts.

evidence.requirement: Sentinel, source data, OS release, and kernel are preserved
evidence.summary: invoices.csv and protected.txt retained their original hashes; RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 remained installed.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 377b5195-7fea-4219-a67b-044ef3f7ab99, received restart scheduling acknowledgement, then observed new boot ID 61583640-bb96-4e00-b731-84a673288284 with sshd active and all utility, data, security, concurrency, failure-atomicity, and cleanup checks passing.
